issues.legal_issue: A bona fide mistake of counsel that causes an appeal to be filed in the wrong forum can justify extending the time for filing it in the proper forum.
material_facts: The suit’s original valuation placed the appeal in the High Court, but counsel valued the appeal below the threshold and filed it in the District Court.
Counsel’s error was attributed to a genuine misunderstanding of a court rule concerning the forum for appeals in suits for accounts.
The memorandum disclosed both the original suit valuation and the appeal valuation, and the appellant paid the court fee that would have been payable in the High Court.
The appeal was filed in the High Court on the day it was returned by the District Court, and the record disclosed no underhand motive or attempt to evade limitation.
Counsel continued to act on the same understanding in seeking revision of the District Court’s order.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should have extended time under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908; its order was set aside and the appeal was remitted for hearing and disposal according to law.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908, a mistake by counsel may justify condoning delay in appropriate circumstances, but counsel’s mistake is not by itself sufficient. The court must assess whether it was bona fide or a device to conceal an ulterior purpose, such as a litigant’s laches or an attempt to evade limitation. The court relied on section 39(1) of the Punjab Courts Act and Rule 4 in Chapter 3-B of Volume I of the High Court Rules and Orders to assess the asserted mistake. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: appeal_requires_delay_extension and appeal_filed_in_wrong_forum_on_counsel_advice and counsel_mistake_was_bona_fide and no_ulterior_motive and appeal_valuation_was_disclosed

predicates.appeal_requires_delay_extension: The litigant sought additional time because the appeal was not filed in the proper forum within the applicable period.
predicates.appeal_filed_in_wrong_forum_on_counsel_a: Counsel filed the appeal in a forum that lacked jurisdiction, acting on counsel’s understanding of the applicable forum rules.
predicates.counsel_mistake_was_bona_fide: Counsel’s error arose from a genuine misunderstanding rather than a deliberate attempt to mislead or evade the law.
predicates.no_ulterior_motive: The litigant did not use the mistaken filing to conceal personal inaction or to gain an improper advantage.
predicates.appeal_valuation_was_disclosed: The appeal papers disclosed the original suit valuation as well as the valuation asserted for the appeal.

issues.definition: When an appeal requires an extension of time, was filed in the wrong forum because of counsel’s bona fide mistake, involved no ulterior motive, and disclosed the relevant valuations, the rule grants an extension.

issues.legal_issue: In a suit for accounts where the amount decreed is below the original suit valuation, the original valuation determines the forum for appeal.
material_facts: The suit included a claim for accounts and was valued, after an amendment relating to ejectment, at a total of Rs. 5,930 for court-fee and jurisdiction purposes.
The amount decreed was below that original valuation.
The appeal was valued at Rs. 4,880, below the threshold for filing in the High Court, and was initially filed in the District Court.
issues.conclusion: Because the amount decreed was below the original suit valuation, the original valuation governed the appellate forum; the appeal belonged in the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: Section 39(1) of the Punjab Courts Act determined the forum by the value of the appeal. Rule 4 in Chapter 3-B of Volume I of the High Court Rules and Orders provides that, in a suit for accounts, the amount found due and decreed determines the appellate forum when it exceeds the plaintiff’s tentative valuation. That rule does not apply when the amount decreed is below the original valuation; in that circumstance, the original valuation determines the forum. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.appeal_from_accounts_suit: The proceeding is an appeal from a suit that includes a claim for accounts valued tentatively by the plaintiff.
predicates.decreed_amount_below_original_suit_valua: The amount decreed by the trial court is less than the valuation of the suit in the original court.

issues.definition: If an appeal arises from a suit for accounts and the decreed amount is below the original suit valuation, the original valuation controls the appellate forum.
